items.title: TwoFactorX
items.text: Add a two-factor authentication to MODX.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• MODX Revolution 2.8+
  • PHP 7.4+

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Add a two-factor authentication to the MODX manager.
  • Secure the front end login with a pre-hook for the "Login" extra.
  • Generate a QR Code for saving the authenticator secret with a snippet.
  • Login into the manager without two-factor authentication until the authenticator secret is verified.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Check the code in the TwoFactorXLogin hook for all users with enabled two-factor authentication.
  • Limit the code attempts and accept each code only once.
  • Don't reset all secrets, if the encryption key is invalid.
  • Remove the secret from the QR code URL and the server paths from the manager.

items.title: Contributors
items.text: The TwoFactorX project was started in 2023 by Thomas Jakobi as a complete rewrite of the GoogleAuthenticatorX package by Mina Gerges.

items.title: Reasons for the fork
items.text:
The primary reason for the rewrite was the usage of an external service to create the QR code. This is insecure and should not be used for sites, where absolute security is needed. The current code uses an internal QR code generation.

The name change was made because the authentication code can be used with other two-factor authentication applications such as Authy, 1Password etc.

The other code changes are the following:

  • MODX 3 compatibility
  • code simplification
  • common code structure for better use of the MODX API
  • rename some system settings
  • use MODX permissions in the user edit page and in the processors
  • use Composer for the third party software

Many thanks to all who contributed, whether by creating pull requests, submitting bug reports, or donating.

items.title: Install from MODX Extras
items.text: Search for TwoFactorX in the Package Manager of your MODX installation and install it in there.

items.title: Manual installation
items.text:
If you can't access the MODX Extras Repository in your MODX installation, you can manually install TwoFactorX.

  • Download the transport package from MODX Extras (or one of the pre-built transport packages in _packages)
  • Upload the zip file to your MODX installation's core/packages folder or upload it manually in the MODX Package Manager.
  • In the MODX Manager, navigate to the Package Manager page, and select 'Search locally for packages' from the dropdown button.
  • TwoFactorX should now show up in the list of available packages. Click the corresponding 'Install' button and follow the instructions to complete the installation.

items.title: Build it from source
items.text: To build and install the package from source you could use Git Package Management. The GitHub repository of TwoFactorX contains a config.json to build that package locally. Use this option, if you want to debug TwoFactorX and/or contribute bugfixes and enhancements.

items.title: Manager
items.text: When the system setting twofactorx.enable_2fa is enabled, the manager login asks for an additional authentication code.

items.title: Verifying the authenticator
items.text: A manager user without a verified authenticator can log in without an authentication code. Afterwards, a window shows the QR code and the secret each time the manager is loaded. The user scans the QR code with an authentication application (i.e. Google Authenticator, Authy or 1Password) and enters the displayed authentication code in the window to verify it. From then on, each manager login needs an authentication code.

items.title: Authentication codes
items.text:
• Each authentication code can be used only once.
  • A wrong authentication code counts as failed login attempt, if the password is correct. After failed_login_attempts failed attempts, the user is blocked for blocked_minutes, like after wrong passwords. This applies to the verify window as well.

items.title: TwoFactorX tab
items.text:
Manager users with the twofactorx_edit permission can manage the two-factor authentication of a user in the TwoFactorX tab of the user edit page. The tab is shown after a new user is saved.

Button Description Change Status Enable or disable the two-factor authentication for the user. Reset Secret Create a new secret. The user has to verify the new secret with the next manager login. Email Instructions To User Send an email with the setup instructions to the user. Email QR Code To User Send the QR code and the secret to the user by email. This is the least secure way to provide the secret.

items.title: User profile
items.text: If the system setting twofactorx.show_in_profile is enabled, manager users can see their QR code and their secret in their user profile.

items.title: Snippets
items.text: There are two snippets included in the package.

items.title: TwoFactorXLogin
items.text:
This pre-hook secures the login of the "Login" extra with a two-factor authentication:

[[!Login?
&preHooks=`TwoFactorXLogin`
]]

The hook checks the authentication code of each user, unless the two-factor authentication is disabled for that user. The system setting twofactorx.enable_2fa does not change that. Because the front end has no verify window, the users have to save the secret in their authentication application before, i.e. with the UserQRcode snippet or in the manager.

It uses the following properties:

Property Description Default twofactorxErrorMsg Alternative error message, if the authentication code does not match. -

The authentication code for the two-factor authentication is requested in the field with the name code. If you add the attribute autocomplete="one-time-code" to the input, tools like 1Password will fill the field automatically.

items.title: UserQRcode
items.text:
This snippet returns the SVG of a two-factor authentication QR code. It uses the following properties:

Property Description Default placeholderPrefix The prefix for the placeholders set by the snippet. twofactorx userid The ID of the user the QR code is created for. Current user ID

The following placeholders are set by the snippet (with the default prefix):

Placeholder Description twofactorx.secret The secret used to create a time-based one-time password (TOTP) in an authentication application. twofactorx.uri The URI used to create the QR code for an authentication application. twofactorx.qrsvg The HTML code of an SVG that displays the QR code that can be scanned with an authentication application.

items.title: System Settings
items.text:
TwoFactorX uses the following system settings in the namespace twofactorx.

Key Name Description Default twofactorx.debug Debug Log debug information in the MODX error log. No twofactorx.enable_2fa Enable Two-Factor Authentication If you enable the two-factor authentication, the manager login is secured with an additional TOTP authentication code. No twofactorx.encryption_key Encryption Key Encryption key that is used for the encryption of the 2FA data. Do not change. - twofactorx.issuer QR Code Issuer Specify the value of the issuer in the QR code. site_name twofactorx.show_in_profile Show Secret In User Profile Allow manager users to see the QR code and the secret for two-factor authentication in their user profile. No

items.title: Encryption key
items.text:
The encryption key is generated during the installation. Don't change it, because the stored secrets can't be decrypted with another key.

If the encryption key is missing or invalid while users have stored secrets, TwoFactorX does not generate a new key. Instead, it refuses all logins that need an authentication code and logs an error. Restore the previous key in the system setting to fix this, or disable the system setting twofactorx.enable_2fa meanwhile to allow manager logins without an authentication code.

items.title: Permissions
items.text:
TwoFactorX has the following permissions for manager users:

Permission Description twofactorx_edit Allow a user to manage the TwoFactorX data in the user edit page.

The permission is part of the TwoFactorX access policy. Assign this policy to a user group in the mgr context to grant the permission. The permission check is not executed for sudo users.
